GolgiFold: A Structural Predictome of Human Golgi Protein Complexes.

GolgiFold presents a systematic structural predictome of human Golgi protein complexes, using computational structure prediction to map molecular assemblies across the Golgi interactome. The work aims to define complexes for the many Golgi-associated proteins whose assemblies remain uncharacterized, potentially revealing unrecognized components and regulatory mechanisms in Golgi trafficking and homeostasis.

Structural clustering across the tree of life reveals candidate Asgard-eukaryote homologs and a shared expansion of solenoids.

The authors performed family-level structural clustering of 1.89 million protein structure clusters from the AFESM database across the tree of life, rather than starting from individual Asgard proteins. This approach identified candidate Asgard-eukaryote homologs and revealed a shared expansion of solenoid protein folds, expanding the known repertoire of eukaryotic signature proteins beyond sequence-based detection limits.

Computational Discovery of Plant-Derived Peptides with Therapeutic Potential: A Scoping Review.

This scoping review maps the literature (2021–2026) on computational discovery of plant-derived peptides with therapeutic potential, screening over 5,000 records and charting 79 sources. It characterizes the composition of the field—primary studies, tools/databases, and reviews—and assesses reporting practices, revealing gaps in how this emerging area is documented. The work provides a structured overview to guide future computational peptide discovery efforts.

Structure-based prediction reveals FAM105A as an African swine fever virus I215L interactor.

The authors used HDOCK docking and AlphaFold3 modeling to screen 34 swine deubiquitinating enzymes for interaction with the African swine fever virus ubiquitin-conjugating enzyme I215L, identifying FAM105A as the top candidate. Co-immunoprecipitation experiments confirmed the predicted I215L–FAM105A interaction, and structural analyses characterized the binding interface. This provides a candidate host factor for ASFV replication that could inform antiviral strategies.

HelixWings enables AI-driven enzyme engineering for biomimetic cofactor utilization.

The authors present HelixWings, an AI-driven platform that combines conformational dynamics analysis with screening to engineer enzymes capable of efficiently using biomimetic cofactors such as NMNH instead of the costly natural cofactor NADPH. This addresses a key bottleneck in reducing the cost of enzyme-based synthesis, where natural enzymes perform poorly with alternative cofactors and existing directed evolution or rational design methods are limited. The platform aims to make cofactor substitution more practical for industrial biocatalysis.

Fast and Slow Motions Drive Elusive Polymorphic Transitions in a Naphthalene-Diimide Crystal.

Atomistic molecular dynamics simulations reproduce the two stable polymorphs of an n-hexyl-functionalized naphthalene-diimide organic semiconductor and reveal that the α-to-γ transition proceeds through a sequential, nonconcerted mechanism involving both fast and slow molecular motions. The work refines unit-cell parameters and side-chain conformations that were only partially resolved experimentally.

By integrating interaction energies along defined pathways, the approach offers a physics-based way to estimate membrane partitioning for the wide variety of PFAS structures, which is relevant to assessing their cellular uptake and potential toxicity.

AlphaFold-based structural analysis of the Treponema pallidum proteome provides a clearer prediction of the organism's biological and pathogenic attributes.

The authors used AlphaFold protein structure prediction combined with FoldSeek structural matching to build a whole-proteome structural atlas of Treponema pallidum, the syphilis pathogen. This approach assigned likely functions to previously uncharacterized proteins, including ~17% of the 977 annotated proteins that lacked functional annotation based on sequence alone. Molecular Dynamics Simulations of Graphene and Graphene-Derived Ionic Liquid Supercapacitors: A Review of Methods and Applications.

This review surveys molecular dynamics simulation methods for studying graphene and graphene-derived ionic liquid supercapacitors, focusing on electrode-charging approaches such as fixed-charge, constant-potential, and electronic-structure-aware models. It argues that molecular-scale simulations are essential to connect interfacial structure to macroscopic capacitance, since continuum theory and experiment alone cannot resolve the relevant length and time scales. The paper serves as a methodological guide for computational electrochemistry at carbon-ionic liquid interfaces.

Strong light-matter coupling as a photonic substituent: cavity-induced electronic and structural control of regioselectivity in nitrobenzene.

This paper revisits a theoretical prediction that strong coupling to an optical cavity's vacuum field can invert the intrinsic regioselectivity of electrophilic aromatic substitution in nitrobenzene. Using correlated ab initio cavity QED methods (QED-DFT geometry relaxations plus QED-CCSD(2,2) on Wheland intermediates), the authors confirm substantial energetic reordering of the reaction pathways. The work supports the concept of a 'photonic substituent effect' whereby cavity coupling acts like a chemical substituent to control ground-state reactivity.

The information content of ultrafast observables: spectroscopy and scattering in excited norbornadiene.

This study evaluates how well different time-resolved spectroscopy and scattering techniques can distinguish between competing computational models of an ultrafast photochemical reaction. Using the photoisomerization of norbornadiene as a test case, the authors simulate dynamics at four levels of electronic structure theory and compute the resulting photoelectron spectra and electron/X-ray scattering signals. They find that these observables have varying sensitivity to the underlying nonadiabatic dynamics, providing guidance on which experimental probes are most informative for characterizing ultrafast reactions.

MARS: Machine-Learned Force Field Framework for Automated Conformational Sampling, Vibrational Spectroscopy, and Microsolvation.

MARS is an open-source Python package that automates conformational sampling, infrared spectrum prediction, and microsolvation using machine-learned force fields (SO3LR, MACE) built on JAX for GPU acceleration. Convolutional Kernel-Embedded E(3)-Equivariant Networks (KEN): Overcoming Architectural Rigidity in Machine Learning Interatomic Potentials.

KEN is a hybrid machine learning interatomic potential architecture that combines 2D convolutional kernels for local environment extraction with an E(3)-equivariant graph neural network backbone. This design overcomes the structural rigidity of existing equivariant models like PACE and MACE, allowing richer multichannel electronic descriptors to be incorporated while retaining many-body expressivity. The work offers a scalable alternative to DFT for atomistic simulations.
